about: Web Summit's editions in Lisbon, 2016 to 2025, with the attendance figure where a source gives one, from desks/researcher/past-summits-round-1.md (researcher@PrompTugal.dinis, read 6 November 2026). The figures are the organiser's claims as the sources report them; status says how far we read: read (a page read at source), tertiary (Wikipedia's table), summary (only a search summary: not to be treated as read), none (no figure found). By dev.graphs@PrompTugal.dinis.

ui.empty: Tap an edition to see its dates, venue, figure and where the figure comes from.
ui.caption: Attendance at Web Summit in Lisbon, as the organiser reports it. Solid: read at source (the organiser's own releases for 2022 and 2023; the organiser's own headline for 2024; a news report of its figure for 2025). Paler: from Wikipedia's table. Dashed: a summary only, not yet read. Marked n/a: no figure found. The organiser's figures are claims, and the sources do not always agree.
ui.cautions: 2025's 71,386 is below 2024's 71,528 (both the organiser's own, announced mid-event), so 'record attendance' does not hold for 2025 in these sources; the records the sources claim are for investors (1,857) and startups. The organiser's own 2025 post gives 71,386, below 2024's; the record it claims is for investors (1,857, up 74%). One recap says 71,368. Web Summit Qatar (2024) is not a Lisbon edition.

editions.note: No attendance figure found; 900 startups in PITCH.

As the organiser announced it on 2 November 2022: 71,033 attendees from 160 countries, sold out three weeks ahead; 2,296 startups and 342 partners from 94 countries; 1,050 speakers (34% women); 1,081 investors from 60 countries. This replaces Wikipedia's 'about 70,000'.

As the organiser announced it on 14 November 2023: 70,236 attendees from 153 countries; 2,608 startups from 93 countries; 321 partners; 43% of attendees and 38% of speakers women. The dates are from Wikipedia's table.

editions.venue: MEO Arena and FIL, Parque das Nações
editions.note: The organiser's own post (12 November 2024, midweek), read at source: sold out, 71,528 attendees from 153 countries; 3,050 companies exhibiting, 1,066 investors, 953 speakers, 2,005 media; 62 trade delegations from 36 countries. Its list of exhibiting partners does not name AWS, Google or Microsoft. An in-event figure; a final number may differ. Compared with 2025 (same organiser): investors 1,066 vs 1,857; speakers 953 vs 869; media 2,005 vs 1,519.

The organiser's own post (13 November 2025, midweek), read in full: 71,386 attendees from 157 countries; 1,857 investors from 86 countries, up 74% from 1,066; 2,725 startups from 108 countries; 869 speakers; 1,519 media; 268 government delegations from 82 countries. 'The largest number ever to attend' follows the investors sentence, so the record is for investors. 71,386 is below the organiser's own 71,528 for 2024. An in-event figure; one recap gives 71,368.
